predecessors.name: Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
predecessors.text: the Socialist Republic of Croatia, one of the federation's republics, whose independence the page dates to 25 June 1991

ledger.x: 1991, 25 June: Croatia declares independence from Yugoslavia.
1991: war over the Serb-held third of Croatia.
1991: Croatia loses control of the Krajina.
1991, October: Konavle near Dubrovnik is occupied by the Yugoslav army.
1991, 19 December: Western Slavonia joins the Krajina.
1992, 26 February: Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Syrmia join the Krajina.
1992, October: the Yugoslav army leaves Konavle.
1995, May: Western Slavonia returns to Croatia in Operation Flash.
1995, May: Flash ends with Western Slavonia in Croatian hands; the page gives the month of the operation, not its last day.
1995, August: the Krajina falls to Croatia in Operation Storm.
1995, August: Storm ends the fighting for the Krajina; the RSK's president's term ended on 7 August 1995.
1998, January: the last occupied land returns to Croatia.

wars.name: Croatian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Croatian victory: Croatian forces regained most of the RSK's territory in 1995; Eastern Slavonia, under UN control from 1996, was reintegrated by January 1998.

wars.name: Operation Flash
wars.outcome: Croatian forces gained control of SAO Western Slavonia in May 1995.

wars.name: Operation Storm
wars.outcome: Croatia retook the biggest part of the occupied land in August 1995; the RSK was disbanded and 150,000 to 200,000 Serbs fled.

certainty.note: Front lines of the war (to 1995) and the UN-administered Eastern Slavonia (1996-1997) are not treaty borders; the Prevlaka peninsula stayed disputed under UN observers (the War page: 'demilitarized and turned over to the UNPROFOR').

The borders are the former republican borders of Yugoslavia, but the Croatia page lists 'unresolved border disputes throughout Southeast Europe' including with Slovenia (Piran Bay); the sea border with Slovenia and the Neum corridor are…
